21 Which region of the electromagnetic spectrum includes waves with a frequency of 107
MHz?
A
infra-red waves
B
radio waves
C
ultraviolet waves
D
X-rays

hints: Notice the given frequency is $10^7 \text{MHz}$, not $10^7 \text{Hz}$ - convert mega to base units first.
Recall the order of increasing frequency: radio waves, microwaves, infra-red, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.
Compare your converted value of about $10^{13} \text{Hz}$ with the typical $10^9 \text{Hz}$ limit for radio and $10^{15} \text{Hz}$ start for ultraviolet.
walkthrough: Identify the given quantity: frequency $f = 10^7 \text{MHz}$ from the question stem.
Recall the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing frequency: radio waves lowest, then microwaves, infra-red, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays highest.
Place $10^{13} \text{Hz}$ on that scale: it is well above radio waves at about $10^4$ to $10^9 \text{Hz}$ and below visible light at about $10^{14} \text{Hz}$.
That interval corresponds to infra-red waves, which span roughly $10^{11}$ to $10^{14} \text{Hz}$.
Ultraviolet and X-rays require frequencies of $10^{15} \text{Hz}$ and above, so they are excluded. This is option A.

A.explanation: A frequency of $10^{13} \text{Hz}$ lies in the infra-red range, which is above microwaves and radio waves but below visible light.

B.explanation: Radio waves have much lower frequencies, typically up to about $10^9 \text{Hz}$, so $10^{13} \text{Hz}$ is far too high.

C.explanation: Ultraviolet waves have higher frequencies than visible light, around $10^{15}$ to $10^{17} \text{Hz}$, so $10^{13} \text{Hz}$ is too low.

D.explanation: X-rays have much higher frequencies, around $10^{16}$ to $10^{19} \text{Hz}$, so $10^{13} \text{Hz}$ is far too low.
